topic.title: Principal Components under Sparsity, Noise, and Constraints
topic.area: Sparsity, Low-Rank Models, and Dimensionality Reduction
topic.overview: Principal component analysis finds directions that summarize variation, but standard formulations can be difficult to interpret or fragile to contaminated data. This topic studies sparse components, robust subspaces, randomized and streaming computation, and decentralized estimation. It also asks where computational limits prevent statistically desirable recovery.
topic.whyItMatters: Sparsity can make components easier to inspect, while robustness can prevent a few outliers from determining the representation. Both introduce additional difficulty. Sample requirements, runtime, and communication cost must be considered together, and lower bounds may apply to a particular algorithmic family rather than every conceivable method.
topic.evolution: A 1992 representative develops outlier-resistant self-organizing PCA rules. Subsequent work adds kernel representations, sparse objectives, and randomized algorithms. A 2022 study establishes strong limitations for sum-of-squares sparse PCA, while 2026 analysis of the accelerated noisy power method relaxes perturbation conditions and supports accelerated decentralized computation.
openQuestions: When do sparse components remain scientifically interpretable under small changes in data?
How close can practical distributed algorithms come to statistical limits with noisy communication?

papers.tldr: Under a stated signal-strength condition, thresholding and a two-stage refinement improve sparse PCA sample efficiency and achieve optimal statistical error.

papers.title: A Geometric Analysis of PCA
papers.tldr: A geometric analysis connects PCA’s subspace estimation error to asymptotic risk distributions and a matching finite-sample upper bound.

papers.title: An Iterative Algorithm for Differentially Private $k$-PCA with Adaptive Noise
papers.tldr: An adaptive-noise private PCA algorithm estimates multiple leading directions while addressing excessive noise and unfavorable sample requirements.

papers.title: Low Precision Streaming PCA
papers.tldr: Quantized streaming PCA nearly attains a theoretical precision lower bound under stated assumptions, with nearly dimension-free error for nonlinear quantization.

papers.title: Nonlinear Laplacians: Tunable principal component analysis under directional prior information
papers.tldr: Appropriately tuned nonlinear diagonal modifications improve spectral signal recovery when directional prior information is available.

papers.title: PCA++: How Uniformity Induces Robustness to Background Noise in Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: PCA++ constrains feature covariance to improve recovery of shared signals from paired observations with structured background noise.

papers.title: Rethinking PCA Through Duality
papers.tldr: A difference-of-convex perspective yields new PCA formulations, explains simultaneous iteration, and supports kernelizable methods including a robust reconstruction variant.

papers.title: Combinatorial Sparse PCA Beyond the Spiked Identity Model
papers.tldr: The paper gives a provably successful combinatorial sparse PCA method for general covariance structures beyond the spiked identity model.

papers.title: Improved Analysis of the Accelerated Noisy Power Method with Applications to Decentralized PCA
papers.tldr: A sharper noise analysis preserves accelerated PCA convergence under milder perturbations and yields a provably accelerated decentralized algorithm.

papers.title: Mean-Shift PCA by Knockoff Mean
papers.tldr: The paper uses deliberately added mean-shift perturbations and spectral stability to identify and remove contamination from PCA.

papers.title: PCA of Probability Measures: Sparse and Dense Sampling Regimes
papers.tldr: The paper quantifies how PCA accuracy depends jointly on the number of distributions and the samples available from each.
